stem: An adult client's blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg. Using current American Heart Association categories, how should the nurse classify this reading?

options.A: Elevated blood pressure, because either the systolic value is at least 120 mm Hg or the diastolic value is at least 80 mm Hg.
options.B: Stage 1 hypertension, because a systolic value above 110 mm Hg is enough to meet the current category for hypertension.
options.C: Normal blood pressure, because both the systolic value is below 120 mm Hg and the diastolic value is below 80 mm Hg.
options.D: Stage 2 hypertension, because a diastolic value above 70 mm Hg is sufficient to meet the current threshold for stage 2 hypertension.

rationale: The 2025 AHA/ACC high-blood-pressure guideline defines normal adult blood pressure as systolic below 120 mm Hg and diastolic below 80 mm Hg. A reading of 118/76 mm Hg meets both criteria, so C is correct. A, B, and D use incorrect category thresholds.
educational_objective: Classify adult blood pressure using current AHA/ACC categories: normal is <120 mm Hg systolic and <80 mm Hg diastolic.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology
source_document_title: 2025 High Blood Pressure Guideline — Top Things to Know
source_locator: Top Things to Know, item 4 — blood-pressure classification framework.
source_claim_supported: Normal BP is <120 systolic and <80 diastolic; elevated is 120–129 and <80; stage 1 is 130–139 or 80–89; stage 2 is ≥140 or ≥90.

source_original.stem: An adult client's blood pressure is 118/76 mm Hg. Using current American Heart Association categories, how should the nurse classify this reading?

options.A: Elevated blood pressure, because either the systolic value is at least 120 mm Hg or the diastolic value is at least 80 mm Hg.
options.B: Stage 1 hypertension, because a systolic value above 110 mm Hg is enough to meet the current blood-pressure category for hypertension.
options.C: Normal blood pressure, because 118/76 mm Hg is below the AHA cutoffs of 120 systolic and 80 diastolic for the normal category.
options.D: Stage 2 hypertension, because a diastolic value above 70 mm Hg is sufficient to meet the current threshold for stage 2 hypertension.

source_original.rationale: Current AHA categories define normal blood pressure as systolic below 120 mm Hg and diastolic below 80 mm Hg. Option C is correct because 118/76 mm Hg meets both criteria. Option A incorrectly calls the reading elevated even though systolic is below 120 and diastolic is below 80. Option B uses a nonstandard systolic threshold to diagnose stage 1 hypertension. Option D uses a nonstandard diastolic threshold to diagnose stage 2 hypertension.
source_original.source_detail: American Heart Association — Understanding Blood Pressure Readings: normal adult blood pressure is systolic <120 mm Hg and diastolic <80 mm Hg; 118/76 mm Hg meets the normal category.
